# overlays


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

All five components float above the page without changing its layout.
Native popovers close on Escape or a click outside them (light dismiss).
While a modal dialog is open, the browser marks the rest of the page
inert. AnswerUI keeps those browser behaviours, applies a shared
floating surface, and places popovers beside their opener. Dropdown
menus use popovers. Tooltips use CSS anchor positioning instead of the
Popover API.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import *
from answerui.demo import demo
from fastcore.test import *
```

## Popover

`Popover` renders a floating panel on the raised neutral surface
(`--color-surface`). Set `popovertarget` on a button to open it. The
browser closes the panel on Escape or a click outside it. While the
panel is open, `mountPopover` sets `aria-expanded="true"` on the opener,
and `Btn` displays its pressed style.

CSS anchor rules place the panel beside the opener and flip it when it
would overflow the viewport. In browsers without anchor positioning,
`mountPopover` computes coordinates in JavaScript and closes the panel
if the opener leaves the viewport. Pass `side` (`'bottom'`), `align`
(`'start'`), and `side_offset` (`6` pixels) to configure initial
placement. `Popover` emits `popover`, `popup`, `data-side`,
`data-align`, and `data-side-offset` for `mountPopover` with no
per-panel JavaScript.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Popover

``` python
def Popover(
    *c, popover:str='auto', side:str='bottom', align:str='start', side_offset:int=6, **attrs
):
```

*A native popover positioned beside its opener by the shared controller*

The shared stylesheet sets the floating surface, viewport size limits,
and entry animation. The browser’s Popover API handles hiding, light
dismiss, and focus restoration.

Set `popovertarget` on any button to the popover’s `id` to open it. Put
ordinary HTML content inside the panel:

``` python
Popover.demo(height='9rem')
```

``` html
<div cluster>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" popovertarget="_dr4rFYQqRe6THR2pNv39Ow">What is a workspace?</button>  <div popover="auto" popup data-side="bottom" data-align="start" data-side-offset="6" id="_dr4rFYQqRe6THR2pNv39Ow" style="max-inline-size: 18rem">
    <p>A workspace holds a team's projects, members, and billing.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Dropdown

`Dropdown` returns a `(trigger, panel)` pair containing a button trigger
and a native popover of links, buttons, separators, and supplementary
content. Pass a label string to create a secondary `Btn` trigger, or
pass a configured `Btn` to control its variant and attributes. Give an
icon-only trigger an accessible name such as `aria_label`. `Dropdown`
always sets `type='button'` on the trigger so it never submits an
enclosing form.

Dropdown items are ordinary HTML links and buttons rather than an ARIA
`role="menu"` widget. Users move between them with Tab and Shift+Tab,
skipping disabled buttons. When the panel opens, `mountPopover` focuses
the first enabled visible control inside it. `Dropdown` adds `menu-item`
to each direct `a` and `button` child and sets `popovertarget` and
`popovertargetaction='hide'` on buttons that do not already have a
`popovertarget`. Clicking a link with `href` closes the panel in
`mountPopover`. The browser handles Escape and light dismiss. To mark an
unavailable item, set `disabled=True` on a button or omit `href` on a
link.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dropdown

``` python
def Dropdown(
    trigger, *items, id:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*A button and its native popover of ordinary links and actions*

The Account example uses a text trigger and starts with the user’s name
and email aligned with its items. The Options example passes a
configured `Btn` with `aria_label`. Tabbing through the items skips both
the static header text and the disabled Duplicate button:

``` python
Dropdown.demo(height='14rem')
```

``` html
<div cluster>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" popovertarget="_rN-Y1tBbTPmBm6NvFsC5Fw">Account</button>  <div popover="auto" popup dropdown id="_rN-Y1tBbTPmBm6NvFsC5Fw">
    <p>Ada Lovelace</p>
<small>ada@example.com</small><hr><a href="#" menu-item>Profile</a><a href="#" menu-item>Billing</a><hr><button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" menu-item popovertarget="_rN-Y1tBbTPmBm6NvFsC5Fw" popovertargetaction="hide">Sign out</button>  </div>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" aria-label="Project actions" popovertarget="_7KxXK8STRYejFizRFL646Q">Options</button>  <div popover="auto" popup dropdown id="_7KxXK8STRYejFizRFL646Q">
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" menu-item popovertarget="_7KxXK8STRYejFizRFL646Q" popovertargetaction="hide">Rename</button><button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" disabled menu-item popovertarget="_7KxXK8STRYejFizRFL646Q" popovertargetaction="hide">Duplicate</button><hr><button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" ui-tone="danger" menu-item popovertarget="_7KxXK8STRYejFizRFL646Q" popovertargetaction="hide">Delete</button>  </div>
```

## Invoker commands

Set `commandfor` on a button to a dialog’s `id` and `command` to
`'show-modal'` or `'close'`. In browsers without native Invoker Commands
support, the shared click handler in `browser.js` calls `showModal()` or
`close()` on the target dialog. Use `popovertarget` for popovers.

## Dialog

`Dialog` renders a native `<dialog>` element with `dialog` and
`dialog-side` attributes. Open it as a modal with `command='show-modal'`
and `commandfor`. The browser moves focus into the dialog, closes it on
Escape, and marks the rest of the page inert. Because the dialog stays
in its DOM position while rendered in the top layer, it inherits its
font and custom properties from its parent element. Close it with
`command='close'` or a `<form method="dialog">`.

The shared stylesheet sets the floating surface (`--color-surface`),
rounded corners (`--radius1`), entry animation (`ui-dialog-enter`), and
backdrop tint. Add `closedby='any'` so a click on the backdrop closes
the dialog. Omit `closedby='any'` on confirmations where the user must
click a button.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Dialog

``` python
def Dialog(
    *c, side:str='center', **attrs
):
```

*A native modal panel, or a full-height drawer at the start or end edge*

The htmx listener in `browser.js` calls `showModal()` on a closed
`Dialog` after htmx swaps content into a descendant inside it. A button
that loads the dialog body with `hx-get` does not need
`command='show-modal'`. Because the dialog opens after the swap
finishes, users never see stale content. Swapping the `<dialog>` element
itself does not open it. A server can send a closed `<dialog>` out of
band to close an open one.

This confirmation dialog uses a `Stack` for its body and a `Cluster` for
its action buttons. Set `aria_labelledby` to the heading’s `id` to give
the dialog an accessible name. The browser does not derive a dialog’s
accessible name from a nested heading:

``` python
Dialog.demo(height='16rem')
```

``` html
<div cluster>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" ui-tone="danger" command="show-modal" commandfor="_pfEaw4L_SSyo29U4tpFu2g">Delete project</button><dialog dialog dialog-side="center" aria-labelledby="_pxFb4NcLSBq1Uj2C68CdEg" id="_pfEaw4L_SSyo29U4tpFu2g">    <div stack>
      <h2 id="_pxFb4NcLSBq1Uj2C68CdEg">Delete this project?</h2>
      <p>Everything in it is removed. This cannot be undone.</p>
      <div cluster class="gap-2">
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" command="close" commandfor="_pfEaw4L_SSyo29U4tpFu2g" autofocus>Cancel</button><button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" ui-tone="danger" command="close" commandfor="_pfEaw4L_SSyo29U4tpFu2g">Delete</button>      </div>
    </div>
</dialog></div>
```

## Drawer

Pass `side='end'` or `side='start'` to `Dialog` to place it against the
inline edge of the viewport (right and left in left-to-right pages). The
drawer uses `--drawer-size` (`24rem` by default) for its width and
expands to `100vw` on viewports narrower than `40rem`. Tall content
scrolls inside the drawer. A drawer opens and closes like a centred
`Dialog`, with the same Escape and page-inertness behaviour. Add
`closedby='any'` so a click outside closes the drawer in supporting
browsers. A button with `command='close'` closes it in all browsers.

``` python
demo(Cluster(Btn('Filters', variant='secondary', command='show-modal', commandfor='filters'),
    Btn('Navigation', variant='secondary', command='show-modal', commandfor='nav-drawer'),
    Dialog(Stack(H2('Filters', id='filters-title'), P('Narrow the list.'),
        Btn('Done', command='close', commandfor='filters')),
        id='filters', aria_labelledby='filters-title', side='end', closedby='any'),
    Dialog(Stack(H2('Navigation', id='nav-title'), P('Sections of the app.'),
        Btn('Close', variant='secondary', command='close', commandfor='nav-drawer')),
        id='nav-drawer', aria_labelledby='nav-title', side='start', closedby='any')), height='12rem')
```

``` html
<div cluster>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" command="show-modal" commandfor="filters">Filters</button><button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" command="show-modal" commandfor="nav-drawer">Navigation</button><dialog dialog dialog-side="end" aria-labelledby="filters-title" closedby="any" id="filters">    <div stack>
      <h2 id="filters-title">Filters</h2>
      <p>Narrow the list.</p>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" command="close" commandfor="filters">Done</button>    </div>
</dialog><dialog dialog dialog-side="start" aria-labelledby="nav-title" closedby="any" id="nav-drawer">    <div stack>
      <h2 id="nav-title">Navigation</h2>
      <p>Sections of the app.</p>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" command="close" commandfor="nav-drawer">Close</button>    </div>
</dialog></div>
```

## Tooltip

`Tooltip` pairs a control with a short supplementary description inside
an inline `span[tooltip]`. It appends the description’s `id` to the
control’s `aria-describedby` without overwriting existing IDs. Give the
control its own accessible name because a tooltip never replaces a
label. Use `Popover` for floating panels that contain interactive
controls.

The description is real HTML shown by CSS alone. It appears immediately
when the pointer is over the control or description, or when the control
has keyboard focus (`:focus-visible`). Clicking the control does not
show the tooltip. Once hover and keyboard focus end, the tooltip stays
visible for `150ms` and then fades out over `--motion`. You can move the
pointer onto the description during that `150ms` delay. Moving to
another tooltip hides the first one immediately with no fade, matching
native tooltips.

`Tooltip` links the control and description with inline `anchor-name`
and `position-anchor` styles. With CSS anchor positioning, the browser
centres the description above the control with a `--tooltip-gap` (`6px`
default) gap and flips it below when there is no room above. In browsers
without anchor positioning, the description is placed above the control
and aligned to its left edge. Tooltips render outside the top layer
rather than using the Popover API. An ancestor with `transform` or
`filter` becomes the containing block and can clip the tooltip.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Tooltip

``` python
def Tooltip(
    trigger, text, id:NoneType=None, **attrs
):
```

*A control and supplementary description shown by CSS on hover or
keyboard focus*

``` python
Tooltip.demo(height='7rem')
```

``` html
<div cluster>
<span tooltip><button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" aria-describedby="__uKZlEmyR62KHRXSNPQ9-w" style="anchor-name: --__uKZlEmyR62KHRXSNPQ9-w;">Archive</button>    <div role="tooltip" id="__uKZlEmyR62KHRXSNPQ9-w" style="position-anchor: --__uKZlEmyR62KHRXSNPQ9-w;">Move to the archive</div>
</span><span tooltip><button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary" aria-describedby="_yNwTBwPnRuu6yyZQynRzOA" style="anchor-name: --_yNwTBwPnRuu6yyZQynRzOA;">Share</button>    <div role="tooltip" id="_yNwTBwPnRuu6yyZQynRzOA" style="position-anchor: --_yNwTBwPnRuu6yyZQynRzOA;">Copy a link</div>
</span><span tooltip><button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" ui-tone="danger" aria-describedby="_jDMk1BskQCavzTk4kJr49Q" style="anchor-name: --_jDMk1BskQCavzTk4kJr49Q;">Delete</button>    <div role="tooltip" id="_jDMk1BskQCavzTk4kJr49Q" style="position-anchor: --_jDMk1BskQCavzTk4kJr49Q;">This cannot be undone</div>
```
